title: Mathematics
subtitle: Textbook for Class X
_direction: sight, this volume's own. The front is one figure from Chapter 9, Some Applications of Trigonometry, drawn as a scene: a stone tower with its gallery and lantern on level ground, and from two points A and B in line with it the angles of elevation of its top, 30° and 45°, with the height h marked. A ground band, a low hill line and two trees place it; none crosses a line of sight. The first version was a bare rectangle and one line, which read as too basic. Dark olive with warm paper ink and a khaki-sand line of sight: no other wrap uses these colours (patchwork's and zoom's pale blues are why the line is not blue). The face is Archivo, vendored and on no other wrap. The back carries the series' words for Class 10 over one plain straight edge that rises to the right. No finish is declared: on a direction the finish is inert.
_spine: pages is measured from a --book run of class-10 (Mathematics I, 14 chapters), with this cover in place so the title page is counted, rounded up to a multiple of four. Get a printer's quote and set spineWidth before press.
